page0.text:
I arrive at my house.
It's well past 1:00 AM.

page1.text:
"Guoh."
A brief coughing fit makes me cover my mouth, and I notice a little blood on my hand.
It still hurts where Assassin punched me, and my back stings where it hit the wall.
I don't know what the internal damage is like, but my back is probably bruised.
Before, I would heal from light injuries right away, but now they don't heal at all.

page2.text:
"Oh, right. I'm back to normal."
My pact with Saber let me heal from all injuries on my own.

page3.text:
That's gone now.
Even a small wound could prove fatal.

page4.text:
"Senpai."
Someone calls me.
Sakura's standing in the hallway just past the front door.

page5.text: "...Sakura? What's wrong? It's the middle of the night. Did I wake you up?"

page6.text:
"I'm up late because I couldn't fall sleep. I saw your shoes were gone, so I wondered if you went out."
"Yeah, I just went out for a walk."

page7.text:
...Oh, right. The lights were on when I got back.
Has she been here the whole time?

page8.text:
"Sakura, were you waiting here the whole time?"
"Huh? N-no, I wasn't.
I...just needed to use the bathroom and happened to pass by the entrance.

page9.text:
"..."
She was definitely waiting for me.
It's been just under 3 hours since Saber and I set out.
Maybe Sakura noticed me leaving right away and waited here the entire time.

page10.text:
"A-anyway, Senpai, would you like some tea!?
I know it's late, but I think you'll feel better if you can relax with some warm tea!"

page11.text:
...
My eyes widen.
Suddenly, Sakura is uncharacteristically forceful.
...I must be in pretty bad shape if she's this worried about me.

page12.text:
"Yeah, thanks. It's good to be back. Sorry for going out without telling you."
I take off my shoes and go inside.
I keep a hand on my hurting stomach and head for the living room.

page13.text:
Sakura steps in front of me.
"Welcome home, Senpai."
She replies, sounding somehow relieved.

page14.text:
"Ouch."
I jump up from the seat cushion my butt is on.
The antiseptic drenching my back burns something fierce.
It even makes a sizzling sound, making me feel like I'm being roasted over coals.

page15.text: "That hurts, Sakura. I don't need the antiseptic, so just dress the wounds with gauze."

page16.text: "I can't do that! Your back is all red, so I have to disinfect it! Of course it hurts, with injuries that bad. Just hold on a little longer."

page17.text:
"Ow!"
...Oof. I wonder if she's this tough on injured people thanks to the kyudo club, or Fuji-nee.

page18.text:
"Does it hurt anywhere else, Senpai?"
"Mmm... No, I only got hurt on my back and stomach. That's all."

page19.text:
"Okay. Then I'll just tape some gauze over it."
Sakura wields the first-aid kit with practiced efficiency.
Her face is stern as she works, and I don't feel like I can interrupt her.

page20.text:
"Whew."
Now, then...
If you're wondering how this happened, it's because I accidentally threw up the tea as soon as it hit my stomach.
I'd planned on hiding it, but Sakura found out.

page21.text:
Then, she pouted until I confessed that I got injured, and now she's treating my wounds.
Of course, she wasn't this aggressive as soon as I got home.

page22.text:
"Eh? Y-your stomach got injured!?"
When I showed Sakura my abdomen,
she blushed so furiously she couldn't even begin to render first aid.

page23.text:
"Are you sure, Sakura? I can do it myself, so you don't have to make yourself do that. Plus, my back is worse."
"I-it's okay! I'll do it! Please, let me!"
She became so flustered that I was worried she would swoon before she could even treat my back.

page24.text:
"S-S-S-Senpai, um, please take off your shirt."
I didn't want to stop Sakura when she's trying so hard, and I couldn't have treated my back on my own.
So, with all that in mind, I took off my shirt and let her work on my back.

page25.text:
My back is scratched all over, and for a while, Sakura didn't do anything.
After staring at each other for a few minutes, she gulped and announced that she'd start giving me first aid.

page26.text:
...
That was 20 minutes ago.
It's now past two in the morning.
Sakura's diligent care is almost finished.

page27.text:
"There, I'm done. I brought you a new shirt, so go ahead and put it on."
"Huh? Oh, you're finished already? Thanks, Sakura."

page28.text:
"No, thank you for your patience."
I put on a fresh shirt and take a deep breath.
I can't do much about the bruise on my stomach, but my back pain feels a little better.
I'll sleep on my stomach tonight. Hopefully it won't hurt as much tomorrow.

page29.text:
"I'd better get to bed, then. Sorry for making you stay up so late."
"Huh? N-no, it wasn't any trouble, but..."
Sakura looks down.
She looks like she wants to say something, but can't.

page30.text:
"Sakura? Did something happen while I was gone?"
"...Um, Senpai, did Saber go home?"

page31.text:
...
I go dizzy for a second.
"Did Saber go home?"
Hearing it out loud from someone else finally drives the hammer home.

page32.text: "Yeah. Something urgent came up, so she had to leave. She won't be coming back."

page33.text:
I push through the dizziness, steady my breathing, and answer calmly.
Sakura has doubts, I'm sure.
Saber was just here four hours ago, so she must think something happened.
So I need to be calmer than anyone and act like everything's fine.

page34.text: "Saber was talking about you earlier tonight. She said that you're too hard on yourself, and that you should lighten up."

page35.text:
"...She did? We just made up, so I'm sorry that we couldn't say goodbye."
I can't even nod.
Saber disappeared before she could say farewell to anyone.

page36.text:
...It pains my heart so much I want to throw up.
For only six days, we worked together.
For only six days, we were partners.
For only six days...she swore to be my sword, and how did I repay her?

page37.text:
"But I'm glad to hear that. You've just been getting hurt since she arrived. Now everything can go back to normal."
"Huh?"

page38.text:
"Isn't that right? I won't ask what you've been up to, but you were going out at night for Saber, weren't you?
Now that she's gone home, you won't have to be in danger anymore."

page39.text: "No. Saber might be gone, but I'm still going to go on my nighttime walks... Um, I wasn't going with her. I asked her to come with me."

page40.text:
I stand up.
I feel less tense now that the first aid is finished.
I suddenly feel sleepy.

page41.text:
"Eh? Sen...pai...?"
"Good night, Sakura.
About that—I'm probably going to be out of the house from tomorrow, so make yourself at home like always.
Make sure you get enough sleep, and don't worry about me coming home late. I don't want you waiting in the entrance all night again."

page43.text:
I can rest my body now.
...I didn't notice before, but I'm seriously exhausted.
Just lying down on my stomach is enough to make my body and mind sleepy.

page44.text:
...
Before I pass out, I stare into the dark, hardening my resolve.
What defeated Saber? What am I supposed to fight?
I need to get that through my head right now.

page45.text:
...
...The memory makes my chest creak.
I tremble slightly, feeling a frustration that goes beyond anger or fear. I feel like my heart's going to break.

page46.text:
"Who...I have to fight."
That Shadow.
That thing out there indiscriminately attacking people.
The black shape that even Saber and Archer were afraid of.

page47.text:
...I didn't see it happen, but I'm pretty sure of it.
Saber lost to that thing.
Assassin couldn't have beaten her.
If anything back there could have defeated her, it had to have been that Shadow.

page48.text:
"..."
I'll defeat the thing that beat Saber.
It isn't my only enemy. I need to deal with Zouken and Assassin, too.
Zouken said that he had no more use for me since I'm no longer a Master.
But as long as I fight in the Holy Grail War and pursue the Shadow, Zouken is sure to appear.

page49.text:
...
...My body trembles.
Saber isn't here anymore.
Without her miraculous healing, I only have my half-baked magecraft to protect me.
I know how foolish and suicidal that is.

page50.text:
"But I've decided to fight. I'm going to be a man who does what's right."
I lost Saber to do that.
It's why I've been following in Kiritsugu's footsteps ever since the fire.

page51.text:
The only choice I have is to stop this war, so that the tragedy can never happen again.
...And that's why this is the last night I'm allowed to tremble like this.
In the morning, once my injuries have healed...
I have to become a stronger version of myself that she would be proud of.
